entities.name: PMID:25445827
observations: Cluster-randomized trial across 22 pediatric practices enrolled 948 families of children aged 3–12 years with persistent asthma; telephone peer coaching lasted 12 months and outcomes were assessed at 12 and 24 months.
At 12 months, coaching produced 20.9 more symptom-free days per child than usual care (95% CI 9.1–32.7), but no overall ED-visit reduction.

At 24 months, ED visits were reduced by 0.28 per child (95% CI −0.50 to −0.02). In the Medicaid subgroup at 12 months, ED visits fell by 0.50 per child and hospitalizations by 0.16 per child; reductions persisted through 24 months.
Authors concluded that telephone peer training reduced asthma impairment overall, with asthma-risk reduction particularly among Medicaid-insured children.

entities.name: Telephone peer coaching
